parameters: It's a display on the flow of seawater.
“Toward the surface, seawater flows\nas currents driven by the winds.”
\bI get all giddy and gooey when\nI see the sea!
\bFor me, Capt. Stern is the number\none role model!
A blue fluid is spiraling inside\na glass vessel.
“This is an experiment to create a\nWhirlpool artificially using wind.”
\bWow, the submarine's awesome!\nI want to go for a ride!
The sea is all connected, but the\nwater seems to differ by region.
\bIf I ripped off the stuff here,\nwould it make me rich?
It's a sample of soil from the ocean\nfloor.
“Over many years, the remains of\nlife-forms settle at the bottom of\nthe sea, making sedimentary layers.
“By analyzing these layers, the\nancient past is revealed.”
“A scale replica of the ship under\nconstruction at Stern's Shipyard.”
\bThe sea is vast without end, and\ninfinitely deep…
\bThere must be many POKéMON that\nwe don't know about.
A red ball is bobbing up and down\ninside a glass vessel.
“This is an experiment simulating a\nWaterfall using the ball's buoyancy.”
\bYes? If you're looking for Stern,\nthat would be me.
\bAh! Those must be the parts I ordered\nfrom Mr. Stone of Devon.
\bThank you! That's great!\nWe can prepare for our expedition now.

parameters.name: ORAS Battle Intro - Team Aqua Grunt (Team Aqua Appears!)

parameters: \bOur Boss wants those parts!\nShut your yap and fork them over!
\bOh, man, what a disaster…\nThe Boss is going to be furious…
\bHumph, sniveling wimp!\nLet me take care of this!
\bNow what? If we don't get the parts,\nwe're in for it!
\bArrgh, I didn't count on being meddled\nwith by some meddling kid!
\bI came to see what was taking so\nlong to snatch some parts, and you\nsimps are held up by a mere child?
\bWe are Team Aqua,\nand we love the sea!
\b…No! You can't be!\nYou're not one of Team Magma?
\bWait, that can't be right.\nYou're not dressed for the part.
\bPOKéMON, people… All life depends on\nthe sea.
\bSo, Team Aqua is dedicated to\nthe expansion of the sea.
\bDon't you agree? What we are doing\nis a magnificent undertaking.
\bAh, fine…\nYou're still too young to understand\nour noble objective.
\bBut, I warn you, don't even consider\ninterfering with our plans again.
\bAnyway, that was a tense situation!\nThank you for saving us!
\bOh, yes, I almost forgot that you\neven brought the parts from Devon!

parameters.name: ORAS Fanfare - Item Key (Obtained a Key Item!)

parameters: \bCapt. Stern: Whoops!\nThere's no time to lose!
\bWe have to set out on our ocean-floor\nexpedition really soon.
\bThanks again, but now I've got\nto go!
\bFeel free to wander around and check\nout our facilities, though.
Does the saltiness of seawater differ\nby region, too?
\bWhat I learn here, I can put to use on\nnefarious deeds…
It's a sample of beach sand.
“Stones from mountains are washed\ndown by rivers where they are\nchipped and ground down.
“They are reduced to grains and end\nup as sand on beaches.”
“A replica of the high-performance\nocean floor exploration submarine.”
\rI think it would feel cool and nice\nto hug.
“When light passes through water,\nmost kinds of light lose color.
“However, blue light retains its\ncolor, making the sea appear blue.”
It's a miniature diorama of the\nHoenn region.
Where is Littleroot Town on this?
\bIf our goons didn't bungle things\nin Rustboro, we wouldn't be here!
A strange machine is rotating under\na glass dome.
Maybe it's for measuring the depth\nof something…
“A replica of the high-performance\nocean floor exploration submarine.”
\bMe? I'm the Team Aqua member\nyou thumped before, remember?\nBack in Rusturf Tunnel?
\bHere, take this!\nYou have to forgive me!
\bThat TM, it suits you more than it\ndoes me.
\bAwww, come on!\nYou have to take this and let me go!
“Seawater contains dissolved salt in\nthe form of sodium and chlorine ions.
“These ions leech out of rocks\nand are carried out to sea by rain.
“The concentration of dissolved salt\nmakes the sea salty.”
A rubber ball is expanding and\nshrinking.
“In the sea, the weight of water itself\nexerts pressure.
“In shallow water, the pressure is not\nvery heavy.
“However, in extremely deep water,\nthe pressure can reach even tens of\nthousands of tons on a small area.”
\bI didn't have ¥50, so it took a long\ntime getting by the receptionist.
\rI want to learn about the sea and\nuse that knowledge for battling.
\bI saw a model of a ship here.
\bIt reminded me of the Abandoned Ship\nnear Dewford Town…
“A replica of a compact, unmanned\npod for seafloor exploration.”
\rWe, Team Aqua, exist for the good\nof all!
“Oceanic Minifact 3\nWhich is bigger? The sea or land?
“The sea covers about 70% of\nthe planet, and the rest is land.
“The sea is therefore more than twice\nthe size of land.”
It's a display on the flow of seawater.
“Near the bottom of the sea, water\nflows due to differences in such\nfactors as temperature and salinity.”
\g\rThe entrance fee is ¥50.\nWould you like to enter?
\rOh? You're with that group that\nwent in earlier?
\rYou're the only one who's late.\nYou'd better go catch up to them!
\g\rOh? I'm sorry, but you don't seem to\nhave enough money.
\rDon't you dare run around inside\nthe Museum!
“A replica of the luxury liner that\ncircles the globe.”
\bWe were told to assemble here,\nso we did, but…
It's a fossil with wavy ridges on it.
“Soil on the ocean floor gets scoured\nby the tide.
“The flowing seawater marks the soil\nwith small ridges and valleys.
“If this soil becomes fossilized, it is\ncalled a ripple mark.”
